Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 670 was a scheduled domestic flight operated by the Argentine airline Aerolíneas Argentinas. On January 9, 1999, the McDonnell Douglas DC-9 aircraft carrying 75 passengers and 6 crew members crashed while attempting to land at the Aeroparque Jorge Newbery airport in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

The crash occurred during poor weather conditions, with heavy rain and strong winds affecting the area at the time. The aircraft reportedly landed hard on the runway and skidded off the runway before coming to a stop in a drainage ditch. The impact caused the aircraft to break apart and catch fire.

Tragically, all 75 passengers and 6 crew members on board were killed in the crash. The investigation into the cause of the crash found that a combination of factors, including the weather conditions and pilot error, contributed to the accident.

The crash of Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 670 remains one of the deadliest aviation accidents in Argentina's history. It serves as a tragic reminder of the importance of proper training, adherence to safety procedures, and thorough pre-flight checks to prevent such disasters from occurring.
